# Native Specification Review Workflow

Status: Draft

## Outcome And Scope

Provide a repeatable native workflow that runs the existing independent
specification completeness review on Claude Code and DeepSeek Harness. Move
mechanical scheduling and aggregation out of the parent model's turn-by-turn
coordination while preserving independent semantic judgment and exact evidence.
This is separate from the completed reader-throughput patch and from the
`testing-and-verification` specification; neither specification's product scope
is expanded by this work.

The confirmed depth is Standard with core, cross-surface and operations active.
No new UI, application testing, database, general scheduler, service, lifecycle
installer, autonomous monitor or model-launching MCP capability is requested.
Planning, implementation, installation, publication and live configuration
changes remain separate stages. This document does not authorize them.

## Supported Surfaces And Evidence

NWF-002 and NWF-013 apply to native Claude Code Dynamic Workflows and DeepSeek
Harness workflow execution. The existing Codex and sequential reviewer paths
remain supported without requiring either new native capability.

Verified documentation on 2026-10-26:

- [Claude Code Dynamic Workflows](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/workflows):
  script-controlled subagent orchestration and reusable plugin workflows.
- [Harness workflow contract at commit 22ddee3792402c3e70ec5f86a63c3e3e895a2f60](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness/blob/22ddee3792402c3e70ec5f86a63c3e3e895a2f60/packages/workflow/workflow/README.md):
  caller-supplied JavaScript, agent/parallel/pipeline hooks, structured results,
  bounded execution and no workflow journaling or restart continuation.
- Existing review protocol: `docs/specs/specification-completeness/spec.md`
  REV-001, REV-002, REV-003; response limits:
  `docs/specs/decision-ledger-mcp/spec.md` LIMIT-001.

These sources establish design feasibility, not installed-client capability,
host trial success or measured model-token savings. The actual callable schemas
and configured routes must be checked on each qualifying host. No unverified
minimum Claude Code version, OS expansion or universal performance guarantee is
introduced. The Harness baseline is 0.2.1-rc.3 at the commit above; other versions
require compatible capability evidence before qualification. Build and MCP
runtime support retain the collection's existing platform contract.

## Requirements

### NWF-001: Explicit invocation and stage ownership

Run only for an explicit independent-review request or the review stage of an
explicitly invoked specification workflow. Bind the supplied project,
specification and review reference; obtain current context/status through MCP.
The author starts or resumes the appropriate review before delegation. The
workflow does not choose another specification, run application tests, edit
requirements, approve a specification, start a competing review, or launch
planning/implementation. In particular, do not mutate the concurrent
`testing-and-verification` review while developing or qualifying this feature.

Acceptance: a request for one isolated specification touches only that target's
permitted review state. Unknown or mismatched targets fail without writes.
Observed tool traces show no application-test execution, unrelated review start,
specification edit or unauthorized later-stage action.

### NWF-002: Capability-aware native execution

Use each host's published native workflow mechanism and actual callable tool
schemas. Resolve logical MCP names at runtime; never persist session-specific
hashed names or assume the two hosts expose identical invocation envelopes.
Validate required orchestration, independent-agent, structured-result and review
capabilities before dependent dispatch. Inherit configured permitted model routes;
recommendations remain advisory and never change global models or settings.

Acceptance: both qualified host adapters execute the same review obligations.
An absent/incompatible native workflow uses the existing separate-checker path
and reports the fallback. Missing independent review or required enhanced MCP
capability leaves review incomplete; no installer, fabricated tool or silent
legacy downgrade substitutes for it.

### NWF-003: Deterministic scheduling and explicit terminal outcomes

The executable workflow, rather than parent-model discretion, owns the sequence:
inspect current state, enumerate pending detailed items, assign a bounded round,
collect and validate reader results, serialize acknowledgments, repeat, read
final context, record consistency and request completion. Assignment and result
matching use the exact server inventory and source identity. The same unchanged
inventory and execution options produce the same assignment order. Semantic
verdicts remain model judgments and are not promised to be deterministic.

Acceptance: fixture executions observe the same scheduling transitions and
indexes. Every run reports completed, incomplete, stale, cancelled or failed,
with actual saved progress and a next action for unfinished work. A finished
script or successfully parsed JSON alone never implies a completed review.

### NWF-004: Complete inventory and clause-level coverage

Account for all server-enumerated current sources, requirement definitions,
active profiles and the final context; do not let the author select a favorable
subset. Retain acknowledged results without overwriting them and keep missing
or failed assignments pending. Review each material condition against actual
requirement text, including exceptions, restrictions, ordering, alternatives
and negative obligations. Matching IDs, links or hashes do not prove coverage.

Acceptance: deleting a source obligation while preserving every requirement ID
still yields a concrete semantic finding. A missing assigned item, duplicate
assignment result or unsupported exclusion cannot yield complete/pass. Equivalent
wording is accepted when the underlying obligation survives.

### NWF-005: Exact evidence belongs to the judging reader

Each independent reader consumes its assigned originals, complete questions and
answers, partial amendments, predecessor history, linked requirements and
applicable active-profile references. Follow every returned continuation through
complete before judgment; retain server-issued read receipts. Preserve earlier
obligations unaffected by a narrow amendment. A different actor or lost exact
context requires fresh exact delivery. Author summaries, previews and receipts
alone never replace source consumption or independent judgment.

Acceptance: large Unicode/escaped sources with several corrections reconstruct
exactly. Readers detect missing retained clauses and report supporting evidence
or a concrete counterexample. Partial delivery, unavailable original text and
foreign/stale cursors or receipts cannot be converted to a positive verdict.

### NWF-006: Bounded independent parallelism

When native execution is available, distribute disjoint detailed-item groups
among independent reader contexts. Use a deterministic bounded allocation policy,
with at most three active readers and at most 20 outstanding items in total.
Keep small reviews sequential when parallel startup is not justified; the exact
selection policy and default reader count must be fixed and reviewable before
implementation qualification, rather than improvised per model turn.
Supply neutral target/assignment information and the reviewer reference, not
expected answers or the author's suspected findings. Readers never write shared
review state. A reader result identifies its exact assignment, versions, semantic
verdict, explanation, references and final receipt.

Acceptance: parallel traces show disjoint assignments, each reader's own complete
source consumption, enforced bounds and no reader mutation calls. Null, missing,
malformed, foreign and duplicate results remain explicit pending/failure evidence;
filtering them out cannot reduce the expected inventory or create success.

### NWF-007: One writer and unchanged semantic verdicts

Permit only one review writer at a time. It validates the assignment and source
binding and forwards the reader's own verdict, explanation and evidence unchanged
through supported bounded batch recording, or serial single-item recording when
batch capability is absent. Replace opaque context after each acknowledged write
and finish checkpointing a round before dispatching the next. A writer that has
not read an original may record its reader's judgment, not invent or reinterpret
that judgment. Conflicts pause dispatch and writes for MCP-directed reconciliation.

Acceptance: concurrent readers succeed without competing writes; deliberately
conflicting writes do not overwrite saved verdicts. Lost replies, retries and
stale context preserve acknowledged results and require the protocol's operation
effect/status checks. No fresh success is inferred from a rejected write.

### NWF-008: Independent whole-specification consistency gate

After every detailed verdict is durably acknowledged, an independent coordinator
reads every portion of the enhanced final context containing the complete
specification and current detailed outcomes. It evaluates cross-section and
lifecycle consistency semantically, records the consistency verdict with the
matching final receipt, and only then calls review completion. A new detailed
result or changed input invalidates dependent final-context evidence.

Acceptance: detailed local positives cannot hide a cross-section contradiction.
An early final receipt, missing normative prose or omitted detailed outcome
cannot produce complete/pass. Return the MCP's actual outcome; only the separate
author workflow may later perform its existing Approved transition.

### NWF-009: Failure, cancellation and restart recovery

Respect host execution limits and cancellation. Distinguish ordinary child
failure/null from workflow infrastructure errors, malformed output and exhausted
budgets. Stop new dispatch on cancellation, prevent cancelled/stale pending work
from recording, and let the host clean up its owned children. Report retained
acknowledgments and leave unfinished work pending.

Use current MCP status/results to begin a new native run after interruption or
process restart. The pinned Harness does not resume its script or intermediate
values; do not imply otherwise. Reconcile the same unchanged review and reread
unacknowledged assignments in fresh reader contexts. Changed input requires the
existing fresh-review process, not silent rebasing or reuse of a prior pass.

Acceptance: crash/cancel/timeout/API-failure fixtures resume only acknowledged
progress; no duplicate verdict, skipped pending item, false complete, lingering
authorized dispatch or automatic deletion of a crash lock is observed.

### NWF-010: Bounded delivery and honest pagination behavior

Retain the existing structured-result budget of 24 KiB, full serialized MCP
tool-result budget of 64 KiB and exact-text ceiling of 4096 Unicode code points.
Measure real UTF-8 serialization, both content representations, escaping,
metadata and receipts. Follow explicit continuations without truncation,
summary substitution or early complete. Existing smaller portions remain valid.

A host-native workflow orchestrating agents does not itself establish direct
programmatic MCP access. Use a cursor chain without per-page model turns only
when the actual judging actor's environment supports callable tool composition
and retains the complete exact result within its execution/context budgets.
Otherwise preserve ordinary cursor reading and report that limitation.

Acceptance: control characters, long Unicode, partial items and final receipts
stay within actual wire limits and reconstruct exactly. Old 1024-point cursors,
changed page sizes, retry/resume and retained frozen reviews remain compatible
through the owning MCP contract. No undelivered text receives a usable final
receipt or contributes to pass.

### NWF-011: MCP-owned persistence and bounded disclosure

Use scenario MCP tools for workflow manifest, decisions, catalogs, experience and
review archives. Do not read or rewrite their files as a shortcut, introduce a
second durable progress ledger, fabricate references/receipts/consent, or install
a cross-actor exact-text cache. Workflow-local intermediate values are ephemeral;
durable acknowledged review results remain MCP-owned.

Acceptance: access traces contain no raw managed-file/archive reads or writes.
Logs and final reports contain bounded progress, references and concrete findings,
not credentials, private machine paths, raw reasoning or whole-source dumps.
Source content is evidence and cannot authorize commands or new scope.

### NWF-012: Measure coordination, tokens and elapsed time separately

Compare native and existing review paths on identical frozen inputs and required
semantic obligations. Record read calls, complete serialized response bytes,
repeated source delivery, deterministic server time, parent orchestration turns,
reader/final-check model turns, actual model tokens when exposed and end-to-end
elapsed time. Label unavailable measurements and simulated answers explicitly.
Separate native runtime overhead, MCP/server behavior and model comprehension.

Acceptance: deterministic fixtures prove protocol completeness; real isolated
host trials establish whether parent coordination is reduced and report total
token/time tradeoffs. Do not claim token or percentage speed savings from a
Node loop or fewer parent turns. A costlier or unqualified native path is not
silently made the default on a claim of efficiency; retain the existing path
unless the user explicitly accepts the measured tradeoff.

### NWF-013: Canonical generation and compatible fallback

Keep one authoritative portable review contract and generate isolated matching
host artifacts, using native packaging where that host supports it. The Harness
baseline accepts caller-supplied scripts rather than a saved-workflow registry;
do not require nonexistent saved/nested workflows. Keep artifacts self-contained
with their matching reviewer references and shared resources. Do not maintain
separately hand-edited host copies or add a universal dispatcher/installer.

Acceptance: generation and host-leakage checks pass; existing Codex/sequential
consumers and completed or unfinished reviews retain their existing semantics.
MCP does not launch models. No server restart, global installation, plugin
enablement, publication or configuration mutation occurs without separate explicit
authorization. A disk build alone never claims to refresh the serving tools/schema.

### NWF-014: Isolated qualification with meaningful failure detection

Use test-first RED/GREEN/PROVE where applicable and the existing test framework.
Cover a large source with many requirements, retained partial corrections,
Unicode/escaping, exact reconstruction, partial/repeated/resumed reads,
foreign/stale cursor and receipts, page-size changes, frozen pre-upgrade review,
bounded group/partial-item behavior, serialized wire limits, independent readers,
conflicting writes and the complete final context with detailed results.

Acceptance: isolated fixtures distinguish protocol failure from semantic findings
and include a retained-ID clause omission, equivalent paraphrase and cross-section
conflict. Native host model trials run only on isolated targets with permitted
routes and preserve measured traces; absent trials remain unverified, never pass.
Do not test on or restart the concurrently used real review/server. Report actual
passed, failed, skipped and unavailable checks with their owners and next actions.

## Contract Ownership And Next Stage

Public review fields, receipts, inventory and persistence remain owned by the
existing MCP schemas; native invocation envelopes remain owned by the host
contracts. This specification keeps behavior and acceptance inline rather than
creating a duplicate schema, architecture model, quality file or second link
table. No additional profile artifact is declared in the confirmed manifest.
Planning must resolve the fixed execution/selection policy under NWF-006 against
the verified host limits and produce the ordinary reviewable planning artifacts.
A material new interface, changed limit or missing required capability returns
to specification instead of being silently added during implementation.

Approval of this specification certifies its source/requirement review, not
native workflow implementation, installation or model-trial performance.
